meaning: SailPoint Identity Security Cloud manages information about identities, accounts and access. Its certification features help people review whether existing access is still needed.
ISC's record for a person or another managed subject. It connects information about that subject with their accounts and access; an application identity can represent a program.
A record used to access a particular system. One person or program can have several accounts, with different permissions on each.
ISC's configuration for a system or collection of account data. The actual application still holds the account and enforces its permissions.
The integration used to read information from a source or make supported changes. Being able to read accounts does not establish that it can remove their access.
An access right represented from a source, such as a group membership. Check what it allows in the application; its name alone does not explain its capability.
A named bundle of entitlements from one source. If the review presents the profile as one item, its decision concerns that package.
An ISC package of access for a business purpose. Its shared definition and one person's assignment to it are different things.
Collecting account information from a source into ISC. It tells ISC what the source reports; it does not itself remove access in the application.
Associating an application account with the appropriate identity in ISC. Inspect the resulting link before using that person's context to judge the account.
Establishing the relationship between a person's identity and their manager's identity using the configured information. It is different from linking an application account to its owner.
An explicit account-to-identity link made through the supported manual process. ISC preserves this link despite matching-data changes; ordinary reprocessing does not prove it was removed.
A source configured to establish identities from trusted information, such as personnel records. Other application accounts can then be associated with those identities.
An identity established from the trusted information supplied through an authoritative source. A placeholder for an unmatched account does not establish that verified person association.
A source account without an authoritative identity association. ISC can still represent it through an uncorrelated identity, and the application account can still hold access.
A record representing unmatched account information. Seeing a name here does not establish a verified link to an employee; inspect the actual accounts and ownership evidence.
An account used by software, such as a program or service. Its human owner is responsible for it, but that does not make it the owner's personal login.
An ISC identity representing a program or service. Related machine accounts can be grouped under it so their access can be understood in that program's context.
A representation of a non-human subject, such as a business application or process. The program, its system accounts and the responsible human are different records.

Putting something into a category using defined rules. Check what is being classified: machine-account classification concerns account type, while data classification concerns information in resources.
Identifying which source accounts should be treated as machine accounts. This is separate from recording an owner or associating an account with a program identity.
A named piece of information on a record, such as department on an identity. Check which record the field describes and whether its value is current.
A named piece of information about an identity, such as department or manager. A department label can help locate the work context but does not justify every permission.
ISC's evaluation of identity information and the relevant access configuration. Check the resulting assignments and account-change work; starting processing is not proof that an application changed.
Configuration that connects an authoritative source with the identity information ISC builds from it. Its mappings explain how source information supplies identity values.
Configuration telling ISC where a value comes from or how it should be used. A saved mapping is an instruction; inspect the resulting record to establish its effect.
A configured business stage, such as Active or Leaver, that can drive access behavior. Its access rules are different from one reviewer's decision on a requested item.
Access assigned automatically under configured business conditions. Review the actual assigning rule when the access should change; a review choice does not establish that the rule stopped applying.
The association through which an identity holds a role. Removing one person's assignment and editing the role's shared contents affect different scopes.
The shared configuration describing a role's access and related settings. A correction can affect several holders, so check both the intended definition and the account outcomes.
Conditions used to determine who receives a role automatically. If the conditions still require the assignment, acknowledging it does not override those rules.
How access was assigned or recognized, such as a request or an automatic role rule. It helps explain what the reviewer can decide and which change can remove the access.
What an account can actually do after the relevant permissions, assignment paths and restrictions are considered. Removing one membership does not establish that every route to a capability is gone.
Configuration allowing certain supported role-content removals to initiate removal of previously granted access. Check the role state, exact change, processing and actual account result.
The organized access-review work with its scope, settings and assigned reviews. A campaign can contain several certifications, each with its own review items.
A review of whether existing access remains appropriate. In this course it means access review, rather than a professional qualification exam.
An assigned review within a certification campaign. Its items, saved decisions and final confirmation are different from the whole campaign's status.
The access entry presented for a decision in an assigned review. Identify its actual account and access object before interpreting the choice.
The person, account or other supported subject whose access is under review. Check the campaign type and the actual record rather than infer the subject from a display name.
The person or supported group assigned to assess review work. Review responsibility does not automatically grant permission to edit an application account.
The actor recorded as making a particular decision. A review's current assignee is not automatically the person who made every earlier choice.
The person responsible for the campaign under its configuration. Campaign ownership, review responsibility and removal work are separate responsibilities.
The person recorded as responsible for a source in ISC. Check the actual campaign or task assignment before assuming that this person received the work.
The person responsible for an access object, such as an entitlement or role. They can help explain its purpose; their ownership label alone does not establish this account's current need.
The person responsible for an account. For a machine account, this is human responsibility for the program's account, not ownership of a personal employee login.
The person responsible for a role. Understanding its purpose and having permission to change its definition are separate requirements.
The person responsible for carrying out or coordinating the required correction. Inspect the actual task and authorized operator instead of guessing from a title.
A configured group of identities that can act in supported review workflows. Its owner, actual members and the person who made a decision are different facts.
Generated review work that an administrator can inspect before starting the campaign. Generating the preview alone does not establish that reviewers can begin.
Creating review work from the campaign's settings and available information. Check the generated accounts, items and assignments against the intended scope.
Starting reviewer work for a prepared campaign through its supported action. A saved template, scheduled preview and active campaign are different states.
A configured condition that includes or excludes supported review content. Check which records it tests and what the generated campaign actually contains.
Reusable campaign configuration. It describes how work should be prepared; it is different from a generated campaign containing assigned reviews.
The people, accounts, access and time covered by the particular requirement or observation. A result supports a conclusion only within the scope it actually checked.
Accept keeping the reviewed access under the established current need. It does not grant a missing replacement permission or repair an incorrect account link.
Record that the reviewed access should be removed. The final review, required removal work and verified application result are separate checkpoints.
Record examination of access whose assigning rule controls the holding, such as an automatically assigned role. It does not override that rule or remove the access.
The reviewer's final confirmation of their review decisions. Saving an item choice and signing off the assigned review are separate actions.
Transferring review responsibility through the supported process. It does not change account ownership or application permissions.
The work needed to carry out a review's required removal or correction. A task status must still be connected with evidence of the intended account result.
Work that creates or changes accounts or access in another system through a supported integration. Reading account data is a different operation.
Work that removes accounts or access through the supported process. Establish the exact required change; removing one permission is different from deleting the whole account.
The place where an assigned worker can inspect and handle supported work items. Read the actual task's account, instructions and assignment before acting.
Establishing who is connecting, using credentials such as an account or token. Successful authentication does not establish permission to perform every operation.
Permission to perform an action or use access. The reviewer's ISC permission, an integration's application permission and the user's business authorization are separate checks.
The supported collection of activity information for use as context in ISC. Check the connector, configuration, event meaning and coverage before interpreting a blank or zero result.
Information about observed actions associated with a source. A sign-in does not establish use of every permission, and recent use does not establish continuing authorization.
A record of an observed action, such as a sign-in, with information about who acted and when. Its meaning and covered period limit what it can establish.
A suggestion to help assess existing access in a supported review. Inspect its reasons and the person's current work; the suggestion does not make the human decision.
A comparison group identified through similarities in identity and access information. Similar people's access can suggest a question to investigate, but does not prove this person's need.
Four selected identity attributes used by supported AI features. Their configuration is shared, so changing them is broader than repairing one missing recommendation.
Access allowing sensitive actions or access to sensitive information. Confirm the actual capability and current need rather than decide from the flag alone.
Information about how an entitlement's privilege has been categorized. An absent or unset classification does not establish that the underlying access is harmless.
An indicator drawing attention to information about reviewed access. Read its exact meaning; it does not supply the person's current business justification.
A flag meaning that the access has not previously been certified. It does not tell you when the application granted it.
An indicator that access relates to cloud infrastructure. Available detail still depends on the supported cloud setup and viewing permission.
Cloud Infrastructure Entitlement Management, which provides information about access to cloud resources. Check the collected permissions, resource and restrictions for the actual account.
Something in the cloud that permissions allow an account to use, such as a database or storage bucket. It is different from the entitlement being reviewed.
The connected entitlements, groups, policies or other objects through which an account reaches a cloud resource. Check whether another authorized path remains after removal.
The cloud path from the entitlement under review to the selected resource. It answers a narrower question than all paths through the identity's entitlements.
The available paths across the identity's entitlements to the selected cloud resource. Check each path's actual account before treating them as one account's permissions.
SailPoint's capability for understanding organizational data and access to it. Classification information and the account's actual permission are different evidence.
Examining data and applying categories using configured rules. It identifies information found in resources; it does not authorize a particular person to read it.
A label applied through classification, such as Health Information. Confirm which resource and data the result concerns.
Configuration organizing the rules used to identify and categorize data. It helps explain the classification, rather than this person's business need.
A High, Medium or Low indicator based on data sensitivity and occurrences. It draws attention to exposure; a High score alone does not mean the person's access is unjustified.
An interface through which software requests information or operations. Check the particular operation's permissions and returned scope.
The address for a particular API operation. Use the ID of the object that operation expects, such as a certification rather than its campaign.
The read operation used to retrieve information in the API examples. A successful read does not save decisions, sign off a review or change application access.
What software asks an interface to return or do. In an access-request workflow, the term instead concerns asking for access; identify the context.
What the service sends back for a request. Read its status and contents before deciding what result was established.
Information carried alongside an API request or response. Some operations require an experimental-use header; a count header describes the request's matching records.
A value supplied with a read request to control its conditions or returned portion. Different operations support different parameters.
Returning a collection of records in portions called pages. Reading the first portion does not establish the complete result.
The maximum number of records requested per page on an operation that supports it. It is different from the number of matching records in the whole collection.
The number of matching records to skip from the start, beginning at zero. With limit two, offsets zero, two and four retrieve successive portions of an unchanged collection.
A response header giving the matching total when requested through a supported count option. It retains the request's filters and caller scope.
A supported ordering for returned records. Consistent ordering helps compare pages but does not freeze records while they change.
Comparing expected records with actual records and explaining differences. Matching row totals alone cannot establish that the right accounts and permissions were included.
The independently checked records the requirement says should be included. Copying an incomplete first response would also copy its omissions.
The organization-administrator role label used by the documented API. Use the specific operation's authorization rules; the label alone does not establish a complete campaign result.
The certification-administrator role label used by the documented API. Check the actual operation and review scope before relying on access.
A label on the next-generation APIs used in this course. Check the current supported operation, availability and required experimental-use header before using it.
The older certification experience alongside the newer campaign engine. Follow the controls and behavior documented for the actual campaign path.
Software running on the organization's infrastructure to support applicable integrations. Its role depends on the connector and configuration being used.
Asking for access through the supported request process. Approval explains whether it should be granted; provisioning and account checks establish the resulting access.
Account collection that can skip further processing of unchanged records. A skipped account does not have its correlation reevaluated simply because the matching settings changed.
The supported collection path that reexamines unchanged account records for correlation. It does not remove a persistent manual account-to-identity link.
A review of a role's shared design and contents. It asks whether the package is appropriate, rather than whether one person should keep their assignment.
